newsitem.title: UK: Cheap, effective vaccine for cholera found.
newsitem.headline: Cheap, effective vaccine for cholera found.

text.p: Researchers working in Vietnam reported on Friday that they had found a cheap and effective vaccine against cholera that could offer hope to developing countries plagued by the killer disease.

Dr John Clemens of the National Institute of Child Health in Maryland, working with a team from the National Institute of Hygiene and Epidemiology in Hanoi, found the vaccine reduced cases of cholera by 60 percent.
The vaccine costs only about 10 cents a dose, does not need refrigeration, is well-adapted to use in field conditions and seems to work well in young children, Clemens' group found.
"Among individuals who received the full two-dose regimen of the vaccine, protective efficacy was estimated to be 66 percent," they wrote in a report in the Lancet medical journal.

During a recent outbreak of cholera in the city of Hue, more than 67,000 people were given the vaccine and another 67,000 did not get it. There were 37 cases of cholera among people who were vaccinated and 92 among the non-vaccinated group.
Cholera is a recurrent problem in developing countries.
In Vietnam, more than 3,000 people a year get cholera and about 30 die from it.
The disease kills by causing severe diarrhoea. It is passed through infected human excrement -- usually in drinking water.
Two types of cholera vaccine can be given orally.
One -- the type used by Clemens's group -- involves killing the cholera bacteria and then using it to stimulate the body's immune system.
Another involves attenuating or weakening the bacteria. But this usually expensive and developing and delivering it is usually out of the reach of the poor countries affected by cholera.
Clemens's group and other experts said the vaccine they used could offer hope.

"An inexpensive, locally produced and effective oral cholera vaccine may be within reach of the limited health-care budgets of poor countries with endemic cholera," they said but stressed that someone else should duplicate the experiment.
